# neo4j-cli

> A super CLI for Neo4j. Team up with your agents to build graph apps from your terminal.

neo4j-cli is an open-source command-line tool for managing Neo4j resources, executing Cypher queries via the Bolt protocol, and integrating with AI agent frameworks (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Cline, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Junie).

## Installation

```bash
pipx install neo4j-cli
```

or via npm:

```bash
npm install -g @neo4j-labs/cli
```

## Command surface

- `neo4j-cli credential aura-client add` — store Aura Console API credentials (client ID + secret)
- `neo4j-cli credential dbms add` — store Neo4j Bolt connection profiles for reuse via `--credential`
- `neo4j-cli credential embed add` — store embedding-provider credentials (openai, ollama, huggingface)
- `neo4j-cli aura organization list` / `aura project list --organization-id <org-id>` — discover the org/project IDs that scope every other Aura command
- `neo4j-cli aura workspace use <org-id>/<project-id> --rw` — pin a default org+project pair so `--organization-id` / `--project-id` can be omitted
- `neo4j-cli aura instance list` — list Aura instances (table or JSON; needs an explicit `--organization-id` + `--project-id` unless a workspace is pinned)
- `neo4j-cli aura instance create` — provision a new Aura instance (`--name` optional; auto-generates `InstanceNN` if omitted)
- `neo4j-cli aura instance get <id>` — get instance details
- `neo4j-cli aura agent list|get|create|update|replace|delete|invoke` — manage Aura Agents (LLM assistants bound to a database); `--tools` accepts a JSON array of `{type, name, description, config}` with camelCase types (`text2cypher`, `cypherTemplate`, `similaritySearch`)
- `neo4j-cli docker create|list|get|start|stop|delete` — run a local Neo4j container by shelling out to `docker` (or `podman` aliased to `docker`); persistent flow stores a `dbms` credential, ephemeral flow emits an env-file consumable by `query --env`
- `neo4j-cli desktop install|list|doctor` — manage a local Neo4j Desktop 2 install: install the app, list managed DBMSes + saved connections, run a structured health check
- `neo4j-cli desktop dbms list|create|start|stop|delete` — lifecycle local DBMSes under Neo4j Desktop 2 (enterprise-only; one DBMS runs at a time on port 7687); `--wait` blocks until `status=started`
- `neo4j-cli desktop dbms plugin available|list|install|uninstall` — manage plugins on a Desktop DBMS
- `neo4j-cli desktop connection list|create|update|delete` — register saved remote DB connection profiles with Desktop; consume via `query --credential desktop-connection:<uuid>`
- `neo4j-cli query --credential desktop` — query the currently-running Desktop DBMS without restating URI / username / password (credential is read from Desktop's safeStorage on demand and never written to `~/.neo4j/cli/credentials.json`)
- `neo4j-cli query <cypher>` — run Cypher against any Neo4j via the Bolt protocol
- `neo4j-cli query :schema` — introspect node labels, rel types, properties
- `neo4j-cli query :embed [text]` — compute an embedding vector standalone (no Bolt connection)
- `neo4j-cli query --param NAME:embed=<text>` — bind an inline-embedded vector parameter
- `neo4j-cli query 'CREATE ...' --rw` — write operations require `--rw`
- `neo4j-cli skill install` — install the agent skill bundle into your AI assistant
- `neo4j-cli skill list` — list supported agents and per-agent install state
- `neo4j-cli skill check` — verify installed bundles for version drift
- `neo4j-cli skill print` — preview the embedded SKILL.md before installing
- `neo4j-cli skill remove` — remove an installed bundle (idempotent)
- `neo4j-cli agent-context` — emit the full CLI command tree as a stable JSON envelope (commands, flags, exit codes, output formats) for AI-agent discovery; `--format` toon/table/json supported
- `neo4j-cli update` — self-update the binary to the latest GitHub release (`update check` subcommand to report availability without downloading, `--pre-releases` for alpha/beta/rc, `--version <tag>` to pin)

## Connection

Connection precedence: flag → environment variable → `.env` file → stored default.

Default URI: `neo4j://localhost:7687`, username: `neo4j`, database: `neo4j`.

`http://` and `https://` URIs are auto-rewritten to `neo4j://<host>:7687` and `neo4j+s://<host>:7687` respectively (path/query stripped). For self-signed certs use `neo4j+ssc://`.

## Output formats

All read commands support `--format json|table|toon`. Default is `table` on a TTY, `json` when piped. `toon` is a compact agent-friendly format; agents are nudged to prefer it. (`-f` is the shorthand for `neo4j-cli update --force`, not `--format`.)

JSON envelope: `{"columns": [...], "rows": [{"<col>": <value>, ...}, ...], "truncated": false, "arrays_truncated": 0}` — `rows` are column-keyed objects; `arrays_truncated` is the count of cell arrays elided by `--truncate-arrays-over`.

## Agent skills

neo4j-cli ships with a built-in agent skill bundle that teaches AI assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) how to drive the CLI. Install with:

```bash
neo4j-cli skill install --rw
```

Or auto-install at CLI install time by prefixing any installer (curl, PowerShell, Homebrew, npm) with `NEO4J_CLI_AUTO_INSTALL_SKILL=1`. Strictly opt-in; any failure is suppressed so the binary install always succeeds.

Installed skill bundles are auto-refreshed in the background whenever the binary version changes, so agents always get up-to-date tool documentation without manual reinstall. Disable with `neo4j-cli config set skill-auto-refresh false --rw`.

`--rw` is required for any command that mutates state (Aura API, local config, credentials, skills, write Cypher) when running under an agent harness or non-interactive script. In an interactive terminal `--rw` is auto-applied — humans typing at a prompt don't need the flag. Read-only commands (`skill list`, `skill check`, `skill print`, `query <read>`, `aura instance list`) never need it.

Additional Neo4j skills for AI agents: https://github.com/neo4j-contrib/neo4j-skills
